subtitle: A Tibetan Pilgrim Among Fallen Viharas

panels.shot: wide, low-angle shot of ruined Nalanda towers silhouetted against a hazy sky, with two robed figures tiny in the foreground
panels.action: Dharmasvamin and Rahula Śrībhadra stand amid charred brick ruins of Nalanda, one young and travel-worn, the other bent with age, framed by blackened stupas and collapsed halls.

dialogue.text: Four decades after Bakhtiyar Khalji’s fiery raids, Tibetan pilgrim Dharmasvamin reaches shattered Nalanda and finds, not empty ashes, but an old master and a last, fragile circle of learning.

i18n.hi: बख्तियार खिलजी के अग्नि हमलों के चार दशक बाद, तिब्बती यात्री धर्मस्वामिन टूटे नालंदा पहुँचता है—और राख में खालीपन नहीं, एक वृद्ध आचार्य और आखिरी नाज़ुक मंडली पाता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Dharmasvamin’s determined face as he studies a worn palm-leaf manuscript by a flickering lamp
panels.action: Dharmasvamin sits in a modest Tibetan monastery cell, poring over palm-leaf texts and listening to elders speak of Nalanda, his features lit by lamplight and full of intent.

dialogue.text: In the high monasteries of Tibet, Dharmasvamin hears of Nalanda—the famed Indian university of the old Pala kings, now spoken of in whispers as broken, burned, perhaps gone.

i18n.hi: तिब्बत के ऊँचे विहारों में धर्मस्वामिन नालंदा का नाम सुनता है—पुराने पाल राजाओं की मशहूर भारतीय विश्वविद्यालय, अब टूटे, जले, शायद मिटे हुए की फुसफुसाहट भर।

panels.shot: wide shot of caravan moving across a dusty north Indian plain, with Dharmasvamin riding alongside traders
panels.action: Dharmasvamin travels with a caravan across the Gangetic plain, prayer beads in hand, passing scattered villages and distant fortifications under a pale, smoky sky.

dialogue.text: He sets out for the Ganga lands around 1234, crossing plains now ruled by new sultans, where rumours speak of horse-riding Khalji armies and ruined viharas in Bihar.

i18n.hi: वह लगभग १२३४ में गंगा-प्रदेश की ओर निकलता है, उन मैदानों से होकर जहाँ नए सुल्तान राज करते हैं, और अफवाहें घुड़सवार खिलजी फौजों व बिहार के उजड़े विहारों की बात करती हैं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the Mangala Gauri hill at Gaya with scattered shrines and pilgrims, Dharmasvamin a small figure climbing
panels.action: Dharmasvamin climbs the sacred hill near Gaya, surrounded by scattered shrines and local pilgrims, pausing to look eastward toward the lands where Nalanda once thrived.

dialogue.text: At Gaya and Bodhgaya he sees signs of decline—few monks, more lay pilgrims—but still living worship. Nalanda lies further, its fate less certain, its name a test for his faith.

i18n.hi: गया और बोधगया में उसे पतन के निशान दिखते हैं—कम भिक्षु, ज़्यादा गृहस्थ तीर्थयात्री—पर पूजा अब भी ज़िंदा है। नालंदा आगे है, उसकी दशा अनजानी, उसका नाम उसके विश्वास की परीक्षा।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of Odantapuri’s hilltop ruins with smoke stains, Dharmasvamin approaching cautiously from below
panels.action: Dharmasvamin approaches the ruined heights of Odantapuri, broken walls and blackened towers looming above terraced houses, signs of old fire etched into stone.

dialogue.text: In Bihar he hears of Odantapuri, once a great monastery-city. Minhaj-i-Siraj later records how Bakhtiyar Khalji sacked it—its stronghold stormed, its defenders and monks destroyed.

i18n.hi: बिहार में वह उदंतपुरी का नाम सुनता है, जो कभी विशाल विहार-नगर था। मिनहाज-ए-सिराज़ बाद में लिखता है कि बख्तियार खिलजी ने इसे लूटा—दुर्ग टूटा, रक्षक और भिक्षु काट डाले गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dharmasvamin speaking with wary local villagers at the edge of ruined monastic walls
panels.action: Dharmasvamin stands at the edge of ruined Odantapuri walls, listening intently as village elders gesture at the destruction and speak of horsemen, fire, and the monastery’s fall.

dialogue.text: Local memories echo the chronicle: mounted troops, sudden assault, flames, monasteries stripped of wealth. Buddhist institutions, once backed by Pala kings, had become exposed targets.

i18n.hi: स्थानीय यादें भी वही कहानी सुनाती हैं: घुड़सवार दस्ते, अचानक धावा, लपटें, और संपत्ति से खाली किए गए विहार। पाल राजाओं की छत्रछाया वाली बौद्ध संस्थाएँ अब खुले निशाने बन चुकी थीं।

panels.shot: long shot of Dharmasvamin walking alone along a dirt track toward Nalanda’s mounds, the horizon hazy
panels.action: Dharmasvamin walks along a dusty track toward low brick mounds and shattered stupas, his figure small against the silent expanse of Nalanda’s ruins.

dialogue.text: Then he turns north-west, following names half-lost in speech, until the great compound of Nalanda rises before him—not as soaring halls, but as scorched brick and fallen towers.

i18n.hi: फिर वह उत्तर-पश्चिम मुड़ता है, आधा खोए नामों का पीछा करते हुए, जब तक नालंदा का विशाल परिसर सामने उठता है—ऊँचे प्रांगणों की तरह नहीं, जली ईंटों और गिरे तोरों की तरह।

panels.shot: wide ground-level shot moving through charred, collapsed halls of Nalanda with Dharmasvamin stepping carefully
panels.action: Dharmasvamin threads his way through corridors choked with rubble, charred wall faces and collapsed roofs, the remnants of carved stone and niches hinting at the monastery’s former richness.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists later see in these layers signs of catastrophic burning. Dharmasvamin sees it with his own eyes: ceilings gone, many houses empty, the great libraries silent and dark.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्वविद बाद में इन परतों में भीषण आग के निशान पढ़ेंगे। धर्मस्वामिन तो उन्हें सामने देखता है: छतें गायब, कई भवन सूने, महान पुस्तकालय सन्नाटे और अँधेरे में डूबे।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside a small surviving hall where Rahula Śrībhadra sits teaching a handful of students
panels.action: Inside a modest surviving hall, the aged Rahula Śrībhadra sits on a simple seat, a few students before him, with Dharmasvamin entering in astonishment at this pocket of discipline amid ruin.

dialogue.text: But Nalanda is not empty. In one hall, Dharmasvamin finds Rahula Śrībhadra—the old abbot, now frail, still teaching a handful of students amid ruin, keeping Vinaya discipline alive.

i18n.hi: पर नालंदा खाली नहीं है। एक प्रांगण में धर्मस्वामिन राहुल श्रीभद्र से मिलता है—वृद्ध महंत, अब कमजोर, पर अब भी कुछ शिष्यों को बीच उजाड़ के पढ़ाते हुए, विनय की रीति बचाए हुए।

panels.shot: close-up on Rahula Śrībhadra’s lined face as he gestures calmly, with Dharmasvamin bowing in respect
panels.action: Rahula Śrībhadra raises a thin hand in welcome, his lined face composed, as Dharmasvamin bows deeply and touches the ground, eyes bright with reverence and grief.

dialogue.speaker: Rahula Śrībhadra
dialogue.text: The halls may fall, son, but the precepts do not fall so easily.

i18n.hi: भवन गिर सकते हैं बेटा, पर नियम इतनी आसानी से नहीं गिरते।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modest patron, Jayadeva, speaking with Dharmasvamin and Rahula near a crumbling gateway
panels.action: By a cracked gateway, local patron Jayadeva stands in simple but refined clothes, conferring with Rahula and Dharmasvamin as he points to surviving quarters funded from his resources.

dialogue.text: A local lay supporter named Jayadeva helps sustain this remnant. With his patronage, a few cells and halls function, proof that monastic learning clings on through local ties and quiet generosity.

i18n.hi: जयदेव नाम के एक स्थानीय गृहस्थ सहायक इस अवशेष को सँभालते हैं। उनके सहारे कुछ कोष्ठ और प्रांगण चल रहे हैं—सबूत कि विहार-विद्या अभी भी स्थानीय रिश्तों और शांत उदारता के सहारे टिकी है।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Dharmasvamin reciting texts before Rahula and the students in a surviving hall
panels.action: Dharmasvamin sits among the small group, reciting scriptures and debating points of doctrine, Rahula listening keenly, the cracked walls around them a stark frame for living words.

dialogue.text: Dharmasvamin studies there for some months, his biography noting lessons, ordination rituals, and the strange contrast: a once vast university now reduced to a few teachers and scattered pupils.

i18n.hi: धर्मस्वामिन वहाँ कुछ महीनों तक अध्ययन करता है; उसकी जीवन-कथा पाठों, दीक्षा-विधियों, और उस अजीब विरोध को दर्ज करती है—कभी विशाल विश्वविद्यालय, अब कुछ आचार्य और इक्के-दुक्के शिष्य।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nalanda ruins at dusk, with distant silhouettes of armed riders suggesting the new power
panels.action: As dusk falls over Nalanda’s broken stupas, faint silhouettes of armed riders move along the far horizon, marking the presence of the new Sultanate order beyond the monastic precinct.

dialogue.text: Around them, the wider order has shifted. Ghurid and Khalji power presses into Bihar; old land grants lapse; monastic wealth and strategic positions make viharas obvious targets in a contested frontier.

i18n.hi: उनके चारों ओर बड़ा धम्म-संघ बदल चुका है। घूरी और खिलजी सत्ता बिहार पर धकेल रही है; पुराने भूमिदान चुक रहे हैं; विहारों की संपदा और रणनीतिक ठिकाने उन्हें इस संघर्ष-सीमा पर आसान निशाना बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of Dharmasvamin writing on palm leaves by lamplight, with a glimpse of ruined structures outside
panels.action: Dharmasvamin writes carefully on palm leaves by a small lamp, recording what he has seen, while through the window the silhouette of a collapsed tower stands against the night.

dialogue.text: He notes no three-month inferno, no single apocalyptic night, but a landscape of burning, flight, and survival—in which Nalanda is damaged, diminished, yet stubbornly not dead.

i18n.hi: वह किसी तीन महीने की महाआग या एक विनाशकारी रात नहीं, बल्कि जलते गाँवों, भागते लोगों और टिके रहने की ज़मीन देखता है—जिसमें नालंदा ज़ख्मी है, छोटा पड़ गया है, पर ज़िद से ज़िंदा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dharmasvamin taking leave of Rahula Śrībhadra at a broken gateway, both clasping hands
panels.action: At a shattered gateway, Dharmasvamin and Rahula Śrībhadra clasp hands in farewell, the old master seated, the younger pilgrim standing with packed satchel, both framed by ruin and open road.

dialogue.speaker: Dharmasvamin
dialogue.text: I will carry Nalanda’s memory north, just as you carried its rule here.

i18n.hi: मैं नालंदा की याद उत्तर ले जाऊँगा, जैसे आपने यहाँ उसकी रीति बचाई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Dharmasvamin’s figure receding along the road, Nalanda’s ruins behind, sky brightening ahead
panels.action: Dharmasvamin walks away along the Bihar road, his figure slowly shrinking, while Nalanda’s ruined compounds lie behind him like a broken city half-swallowed by earth.

dialogue.text: His biography, shaped by disciples, later carries this scene into Tibetan memory—a rare, sober eyewitness bridge between the age of Pala-supported universities and their fractured aftermath.

i18n.hi: उसकी जीवन-कथा, जो बाद में शिष्यों के हाथों सँवरी, इस दृश्य को तिब्बती स्मृति में ले जाती है—पाल-समर्थित विश्वविद्यालयों के युग और उनके टूटे बाद के बीच दुर्लभ, संयत नेत्र-साक्षी सेतु।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a charred stupa base overgrown with grass, with faint figures of future pilgrims in the far background
panels.action: A charred stupa base at Nalanda lies overgrown with grass, while in the distant background a few future pilgrims walk the mounds, tiny against the layered ruins and open sky.

dialogue.text: Dharmasvamin and Rahula Śrībhadra show Nalanda not as pure legend or simple end, but as a real place scarred by violence where learning flickered on—reminding us that honest memory holds both loss and survival together.

i18n.hi: धर्मस्वामिन और राहुल श्रीभद्र नालंदा को न तो बस किंवदंती, न ही सीधा अंत दिखाते हैं, बल्कि हिंसा से दागी वह असली जगह जहाँ विद्या टिमटिमाती रही—याद दिलाते हैं कि सच्ची स्मृति में एक साथ हानि और बचाव दोनों दर्ज होते हैं।
